clue.text: B from Armagh

definitions.note: in this puzzle B stands for a boy's name

indicators.note: the name is made from the letters of the place, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone, perhaps a lettered person, hails from the Northern Irish city of Armagh.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme: B stands for a boy's name and G for a girl's. Armagh is a city and county in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle B stands for any boy's first name, and this one is a common male name.

clue.text: Progress to appoint a new educationist

definitions.meaning: to progress in life is to advance or succeed
a school that appoints a new head teacher is getting a head

explanation.surface: School governors move forward by hiring a new headmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on in life is to advance, and a school acquiring a headteacher literally gets one.

clue.text: A stroke of genius; staff spoke of hearing

indicators.note: the phrase is said aloud and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: A gives A; a coup is a brilliant, successful move; a stick is a staff

explanation.surface: An inspired idea: the walking stick talked about the sense of hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: A COUP STICK, said quickly, gives the word; 'spoke' looks like a verb about the staff but signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything relating to sound and the ear's sense, as in acoustic nerve.

clue.text: Lecturer of little importance

definitions.meaning: a merely theoretical point, of no practical consequence

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A university teacher is one sense; a question of no practical relevance is a moot or theoretical one.

clue.text: G having an asthma attack

definitions.note: in this puzzle G stands for a girl's name

indicators.note: an attack throws things into disorder, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A girl suffering a bout of asthma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attack' looks like the medical episode but is the anagram signal for AN ASTHMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle G stands for any girl's first name, and this one is a familiar female name.

clue.text: Examination involving All about Eve

indicators.note: the bigger word goes about, around, the smaller one

explanation.surface: A test paper featuring the classic film All About Eve.
explanation.walkthrough: All About Eve is a 1950 Bette Davis film. An A level is the British school-leaving exam taken at about 18.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the advanced school qualification taken in England and Wales, a public examination.

clue.text: County worker on edge

parts.note: a worker is a worker ant
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A local-government employee perched on a ledge.
explanation.walkthrough: Antrim is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the traditional counties of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Initially Tony Blair distorted such family links

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter
twisted out of shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister bending the truth about kinship ties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes T from Tony, and 'distorted' shuffles it with BLAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ties of clan and kinship are described with this adjective, so such links are of that kind.

clue.text: Makes up for what happens at noon

definitions.meaning: corrects or revises, as a text is put right
at midday the morning hours, a.m., end

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what compensates for midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as AM ENDS: the morning finishes at noon.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a text right is to revise it; at twelve o'clock the morning period finishes.

clue.text: B getting zero in maths debacle

definitions.note: in this puzzle B stands for a boy's name

indicators.note: the round letter goes in among the jumbled letters of the school subject
a debacle is a fiasco or collapse, so the letters of maths are thrown into disorder

parts.note: zero is the round letter O

explanation.surface: A boy scores nought in a maths exam that went badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Debacle' rearranges MATHS into THMAS, and 'in' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle B stands for any boy's first name, and this is a common male name.

clue.text: G will live for a moment

definitions.note: in this puzzle G stands for a girl's name

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
a trice is an instant, as in 'in a trice'

explanation.surface: A girl who will only survive for a brief instant.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'be a trice': to live for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle G stands for any girl's first name, and this one is a traditional female name.

clue.text: G from Deva, topless

definitions.note: in this puzzle G stands for a girl's name

indicators.note: without its top, so the first letter of the city's name is lost

parts.note: Deva was the Roman name for the English city of Chester

explanation.surface: A girl from a Roman city, scantily dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Deva is the Latin name for Chester, a city in north-west England; 'topless' takes off its first letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle G stands for any girl's first name, and this one is an old-fashioned female name.

clue.text: B reading Latin badly

definitions.note: in this puzzle B stands for a boy's name

indicators.note: something done badly comes out wrong, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A boy making a poor job of reading his Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' shuffles READING together with L.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle B stands for any boy's first name, and this one is a traditional male name.

clue.text: Once again travelling man receives pay increase

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, travels for work
a rise is an increase in wages

explanation.surface: A sales rep gets another wage rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receives' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat of a musical passage, or a performance given again, is this.

clue.text: See 25 across
G removes head of government from autonomous Spanish area

definitions.note: in this puzzle G stands for a girl's name

indicators.note: the girl's name is what is left once a letter is taken away from the region

parts.note: Galicia is an autonomous community in north-west Spain

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A girl dropping the leader of a government in a Spanish region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of government' gives G, which 'removes' takes out of GALICIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle G stands for any girl's first name, and this one is a Spanish-flavoured female name.

clue.text: Group topped ditch

indicators.note: with its top cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: ...-ha is a sunken ditch serving as a boundary in a garden

explanation.surface: A band's heads rolled in the trench.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunken fence beside English country gardens; topping it leaves the name of the Norwegian band behind 'Take On Me'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian pop band of the 1980s is a musical group.

clue.text: Little G's better half

indicators.note: the first half of the word, three letters of six

explanation.surface: A little girl's husband or partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better half' looks like a spouse, but it is half of the word better.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of Elizabeth, so a pet name for a girl.

clue.text: B without a cleaner, almost

definitions.note: in this puzzle B stands for a boy's name

parts.note: a char, or charlady, is a cleaning woman

indicators.note: almost the whole thing, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: less means without, as in '...', having no cleaner

explanation.surface: A boy nearly left with no one to clean for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a cleaner' is CHARLESS, a char being a British word for a cleaning lady; 'almost' cuts its last S.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle B stands for any boy's first name, and this one is a royal male name.

clue.text: Discharge from TV costs nothing

parts.note: TV sets, or a TV set's, give the word for televisions
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: Release from television comes at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as SET'S FREE: the TV set costs nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a prisoner is to release or liberate them.

clue.text: G — the bird with whom to run off

definitions.note: in this puzzle G stands for a girl's name

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
to elope is to run off to marry

explanation.surface: A girlfriend, the woman to run away with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for a girlfriend, but here it is the female swan.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle G stands for any girl's first name; this one recalls the faithful wife of Odysseus.

clue.text: Old characters in diary now revealing routine

indicators.note: the alternate letters, first, third and fifth, of the word are picked

parts.note: today means now, at present

explanation.surface: Ancient writing in a journal shows the daily grind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' seems to be a typo for 'Odd': the odd letters of DIARY give DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary everyday business is routine.

clue.text: G in residence, having drink brought round

definitions.note: in this puzzle G stands for a girl's name

indicators.note: the drink is wrapped round the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A girl at home, with a drink fetched for her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In residence' looks like a container signal, but residence is the piece, shortened, and 'brought round' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle G stands for any girl's first name, and this one is a saintly female name.

clue.text: Streaks, as a dirty campaigner does

definitions.meaning: a dirty campaigner spreads slurs against rivals

explanation.surface: Mud-slinging politics leaves stains.
explanation.definitionFit: Smudges are greasy marks; a mudslinging politician defames rivals.

clue.text: Laments from those on a lily-pad?

definitions.meaning: frogs sit on lily-pads and make deep rough calls

explanation.surface: Wailing coming from the frogs in the pond.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble gloomily is one sense; it is also the hoarse sound frogs make.

clue.text: B from 6

definitions.note: in this puzzle B stands for a boy's name

indicators.note: the name is made out of the rearranged letters

parts.note: 6 refers to the answer at 6 down, the Northern Irish county

explanation.surface: A boy who comes from clue six's county.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 down is ANTRIM; its letters rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle B stands for any boy's first name, and this one is a common male name.

clue.text: G — aka Blaise

definitions.note: in this puzzle G stands for a girl's name

indicators.note: 'also known as' suggests the same letters going under another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl who goes by the alias Blaise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aka' signals an alternative arrangement of the letters of BLAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle G stands for any girl's first name, and this one is a classic female name.

clue.text: G in the middle of things, riding Mirage

definitions.note: in this puzzle G stands for a girl's name

indicators.note: the central two letters of each of the three words are taken

explanation.surface: A girl at the heart of the action, flying a Mirage jet.
explanation.walkthrough: The centres of THINGS, RIDING and MIRAGE give IN, DI and RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle G stands for any girl's first name; this one recalls India's former prime minister Gandhi.

clue.text: G's husband in Lille goes to bird's heart

parts.note: Lille is a French city, and mari is French for husband

indicators.note: the heart of a word is what is left inside once its ends are trimmed

parts.note: a gannet is a seabird
in this puzzle G stands for a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman whose French husband heads off to a bird's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: GANNET without its ends G and T leaves ANNE, its heart; 'goes to' joins it to MARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle G stands for any girl's first name, and this one is the female symbol of France.

clue.text: B with series of maps having live radio telegraphy in short

definitions.note: in this puzzle B stands for a boy's name

parts.note: OS is Ordnance Survey, the British national mapping agency, whose maps form a series
to live is to be
RT abbreviates radio telegraphy

explanation.surface: A boy with a map collection, broadcasting live by radio telegraph.
explanation.walkthrough: OS stands for Ordnance Survey, Britain's official map maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle B stands for any boy's first name, and this is an old-fashioned male name.

clue.text: B giving his final performance as balladeer

definitions.text: B giving his final performance as balladeer

parts.words: B giving his final performance as balladeer
parts.note: a singer's farewell is his closing song, and an old word for a song or tune is air; said as one run, that phrase is a Scottish boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy singer takes his farewell bow.
explanation.walkthrough: There is nothing to assemble: the clue describes a farewell song, which in old poetic words is a final air, and run together that phrase is the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle B stands for any boy's first name, and this is a Scottish male name that splits into a phrase meaning a farewell tune.

clue.text: B could be Malcolm or Palmer

definitions.meaning: in this puzzle B stands for a boy's name
Malcolm ... was a British composer, and ... Palmer an American golfer, so the name joins either

explanation.surface: A boy who might be called Malcolm or might be called Palmer.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is a surname with Malcolm and a first name with Palmer.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer Sir Malcolm and the golfer Palmer each share this word as part of their names, one as surname and one as forename.

clue.text: G keeping quiet about American money

definitions.note: in this puzzle G stands for a girl's name

indicators.note: the hushing letters go about, surrounding, the rest

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
an anna was a coin of old Indian money

explanation.surface: A girl keeping silent on the subject of dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: An anna was a sixteenth of a rupee, a coin of British India.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle G stands for any girl's first name, and this one is a biblical female name.

clue.text: B reduced sherry — goodness!

definitions.note: in this puzzle B stands for a boy's name

indicators.note: cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Jerez, the Spanish town that gives sherry its name, is also used for the wine itself
'my!' is an exclamation like 'goodness!'

explanation.surface: A boy boiling down some sherry, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' looks like cooking but cuts the Z from JEREZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout this puzzle B stands for any boy's first name, and this one is a common male name.
